<thought>To determine the number of carbonyl (C=O) groups, the IR spectrum is most informative because carbonyl groups show a strong, characteristic C=O stretching band around 1700 cm⁻¹. Measuring the IR spectrum will allow us to count how many such bands are present, which directly gives the number of carbonyl groups.</thought>
